100_000_orders.graph_query_outlook: Current id indexes suffice for NL→Cypher point lookups and scoped traversals. Global counts/aggregations remain sub-second on single-instance Neo4j. Loader row-by-row ingest becomes the operational bottleneck before query-time indexes do.
100_000_orders.index_recommendations: Optional: RANGE index on Customer.country if country-filter questions stay common. Batch UNWIND loader for ingest.

1_000_000_orders.graph_query_outlook: Id-anchored queries still healthy. Global top-customer aggregation scans ~1M PLACED edges — noticeable but usually acceptable on indexed ids + adequate RAM. Product-name filters without an index scan the catalog then fan out on CONTAINS.
1_000_000_orders.index_recommendations: Add RANGE or TEXT index on Product.product_name if name-based joins are frequent. Consider RANGE on Customer.country. Monitor agg query latency; cap NL→Cypher result limits (already 100).

10_000_000_orders.graph_query_outlook: Point lookups by order_id/customer_id remain viable with existing uniqueness constraints. Global aggregations and unindexed property filters become the primary risk — not NL→Cypher quality but Cypher execution time and heap pressure (~26M CONTAINS at demo line-item ratio).
10_000_000_orders.index_recommendations: Require ingest pipeline redesign (bulk load), likely read replicas, and precomputed rollups (orders per customer, catalog stats) for dashboard-style questions. Ticket text stays in Chroma — graph scale does not bound ticket RAG.

loader_note: graph/load_graph.py issues one session.run per row — ~3k writes today, would be prohibitive at 1M+ orders without UNWIND batching or neo4j-admin import.
